issues.source_quote: Поскользнулся, упал... Закрытый перелом... Потерял сознание, очнулся - гипс.
issues.translation_quote: Closed fracture... Lost consciousness, woke up - plaster cast.
issues.justification: Fine as a refrain, but the later pun 'не закрытый, а открытый перелом' is rendered literally and the joke about 'open' fracture (implying hidden contents) is not made clear; the humor weakens.

issues.source_quote: Собака - друг человека! ... Управдом - друг человека!
issues.translation_quote: The building manager is man's friend!
issues.justification: 'Управдом' is a specific Soviet figure (house manager); 'building manager' is acceptable, but the contrast joke relies on a familiar saying and works only partially; also 'A dog is man's friend' rendering is fine. The weak point is the loss of the sharp bureaucratic tone.

issues.source_quote: Пьянству - бой!
issues.translation_quote: War on drunkenness!
issues.justification: The Soviet slogan register is lost; 'Пьянству – бой' is a poster-style slogan, and the English reads as generic.

issues.source_quote: Чтоб ты исдох! Чтоб я видел тебя у гробу, у белых тапках!
issues.translation_quote: May you drop dead! May I see you in a coffin, in white slippers!
issues.justification: The source is a deliberately ungrammatical, Odessa/Yiddish-flavored curse ('у гробу, у белых тапках'), a distinctive character voice. The translation is standard English and loses the dialect marking.

issues.source_quote: Куй железо, не отходя от кассы!
issues.translation_quote: strike the iron without leaving the till!
issues.justification: This is a deliberate mashup of two proverbs ('strike while the iron is hot' / 'don't leave the cash register'). The English calque is awkward, but the pun is not conveyed; the blend 'strike the iron' is not an English idiom.

issues.source_quote: Вы в самодеятельности участвуете? Участвую. Зачем я соврал, я ж не учавствую?
issues.translation_quote: Do you do amateur theater? I do. Why did I lie? I don't.
issues.justification: 'Самодеятельность' (amateur performance groups, often tied to workplace clubs) is flattened to 'amateur theater', and the interior monologue reads confusingly.

issues.source_quote: Не положено, инструкция! Не взял попутных - это не таксист!
issues.translation_quote: Not allowed, regulations! Won't pick up passengers - he's no taxi driver!
issues.justification: Gorbunkov's suspicious interior logic is that a real taxi driver would pick up extra fares; the translation is clumsy and the reasoning is unclear.

issues.source_quote: Лёгким движением руки брюки превращаются... в элегантные шорты!
issues.translation_quote: turn the jacket... into a windbreaker
issues.justification: 'Куртка' rendered as 'windbreaker' is a questionable choice; 'jacket' contrasting with 'пиджак' (suit jacket) is better rendered as 'blazer... into a jacket'.

issues.source_quote: Дичь! ... А под дичь водку не пьют! - А что? Пьют этот... пш-ш-ш-ш...!
issues.translation_quote: Game! ... But you don't drink vodka with game!
issues.justification: Wordplay exists in 'дичь' as both code name for the operation and an actual dish; 'game' is acceptable but the code-name joke and the 'Federal' double meaning are weakened ('Game' as an operation name feels odd).

issues.source_quote: Ну-с, начнём, пожалуй!
issues.translation_quote: Well then, let's begin, shall we!
issues.justification: Minor tone issue only; but more critically, 'Что ей надо - я тебе потом скажу' etc. are fine. This entry is low confidence.

issues.source_quote: Хорошо, что он не контрабандист, симпатичный мужик...
issues.translation_quote: Good thing he's not a smuggler, nice guy...
issues.justification: Acceptable; flagged for style: the register is fine. Low confidence.

issues.source_quote: Такова «сё ля ви», как говорят у них...
issues.translation_quote: Such is "c'est la vie", as they say over here...
issues.justification: 'У них' means 'among them (foreigners)', and the Russian spelling 'сё ля ви' signals a mock-foreign, semi-literate quote. 'Over here' reverses the deictic sense; should be 'over there'.

issues.source_quote: Эти игрушки идиотские! ... Элементы сладкой жизни...
issues.translation_quote: These idiotic toys! ... Elements of the sweet life...
issues.justification: 'Сладкая жизнь' refers to the Fellini 'La Dolce Vita' reference and Soviet moral-panic discourse; the allusion is lost in 'sweet life'; 'la dolce vita' would be better.

issues.source_quote: Что случилось, почему шеф здесь? ... Но у Белой Скалы нет клёва... Клёв!... Клёв будет, это я беру на себя! Клевать будет так, что клиент позабудет обо всём на свете!
issues.translation_quote: They'll bite, I'll take care of that! They'll bite so well the client will forget everything in the world!
issues.justification: The double meaning of 'клёв' (fish biting and the client being hit) is lost partly; the switch from fish to client is not cleanly preserved.

issues.source_quote: Козадоев ... Козлодоев... Козадоев! Казладоев!
issues.translation_quote: Kozodoev... Kozlodoev... Kozodoev! Kozlodoev!
issues.justification: The running gag of Lyolik deliberately mangling the name into 'Козлодоев' (козёл = goat/jerk) is not conveyed; the translation does not mark the insult, and the final variants are not distinguished.

issues.source_quote: Строго на север, порядка... 50-ти метров, расположен туалэт, типа сортир, обозначенный на схеме буквами «Мэ» и «Жо».
issues.translation_quote: a toilette, of the latrine type, marked on the diagram with the letters "M" and "W".
issues.justification: 'Мэ' and 'Жо' are the Russian М and Ж (men/women) signs; 'W' is inaccurate and the comic bureaucratic pomposity is flattened; 'fyr tree' is a stray typo-style rendering.

issues.source_quote: Чёрт побери / Щёрт побери
issues.translation_quote: Devil take it / Dyevil tek it
issues.justification: The password gag depends on foreigners mispronouncing the phrase; 'Dyevil tek it' is arbitrary and the original's 'Щёрт' (clearly Russian-accented foreign mangling) is not matched; also the translator inconsistently renders 'Чёрт' in dialogue between Russians as 'Damn it' vs 'Devil take it'.

issues.source_quote: Дальше следует непереводимая игра слов, с использованием местных идиоматических выражений.
issues.translation_quote: What follows is an untranslatable play on words, using local idiomatic expressions.
issues.justification: Fine as translation; no issue.

issues.source_quote: Как говорит наш дорогой шеф, если человек идиот - то это надолго.
issues.translation_quote: As our beloved boss says, if a man is an idiot, it's for a long time.
issues.justification: The aphorism 'это надолго' is a deadpan quip meaning 'it's permanent'; English literal rendering is clumsy and loses the punch ('it's for life').

issues.source_quote: Облико морале… ферштейн?
issues.translation_quote: Obliko morale... verstehen?
issues.justification: The fake-foreign gibberish is transliterated rather than adapted; minor.

issues.source_quote: Осторожнас...
issues.translation_quote: Carefuls...
issues.justification: The mock-foreign suffix is rendered as an odd English plural that reads like an error.

issues.source_quote: Усё так, как условились.
issues.translation_quote: Evrythin' as we agreed.
issues.justification: Dialect marking is inconsistent across the character's lines ('Allwaysh', 'Thash all', 'evrythin'') and sometimes overdone.

issues.source_quote: Что ты Геша... спасибо.
issues.translation_quote: Come on, Gesha... thanks.
issues.justification: Mildly altered; Senya is touched, not dismissive.

issues.source_quote: Читали в «Неделе», отдел для, дома для семьи...
issues.translation_quote: I read it in "The Week", in the home... family section...
issues.justification: 'Неделя' was a specific Soviet weekly supplement; no cultural cue is given. Also 'Читали' (plural/impersonal) is rendered as 'I read'.

issues.source_quote: Туп лайтэк ту падо ... Нет и всё!
issues.translation_quote: Chiedias brek momen treizi [The ship leaves in an hour...]
issues.justification: Bracketed pseudo-foreign passages are transliterated nonsense with no attempt to keep the comedic effect of invented-language dialogue; low priority.

issues.source_quote: Мы вообще дальше Дубровки никуда не ездили.
issues.translation_quote: We've never been further than Dubrovka.
issues.justification: Dubrovka is a specific obscure place name that signals provinciality; no explicit cue for English audience.

issues.source_quote: Кто возьмёт билетов пачку, тот получит... Водокачку!
issues.translation_quote: Whoever takes a pack of tickets will get... A water tower!
issues.justification: The rhymed jingle (пачку/водокачку) is lost, and the joke of a ridiculous prize is flattened; 'water tower' isn't the same as a pumping station.

issues.source_quote: Нет и всё! ... А они уже давно в милиции…
issues.translation_quote: But they've long been with the police...
issues.justification: Acceptable; no issue.

issues.source_quote: Лёлик, я всё прекрасно помню! ... Упал, выругался... Чёрт возьми! Ух, прости, "Чёрт побери!"
issues.translation_quote: "Damn it!" Oops, sorry: "Devil take it!"
issues.justification: The distinction between the two near-synonymous curses (the password must be exact) is lost in English where 'Damn it' and 'Devil take it' look quite different; also 'fell, swore' ordering is fine.

issues.source_quote: Ну что Вы, время! Время - деньги! Как говорится, когда видишь деньги - не теряй времени.
issues.translation_quote: Come on, time! Time is money! As they say, when you see money - don't waste time.
issues.justification: Acceptable but the chiastic wit is partially preserved only; low priority.
